5.heading: And I:
refs: To represent the power, rapaciousness, and cruelty of Pharaoh, he had been compared to a fierce young lion, and also to an immense, overgrown sea-monster, or crocodile

and here it is predicted that God would cast a net over him, by which many companies of people should drag him out of his rivers, and cast him into the open field, mountains, valleys, etc., to be devoured by birds and beasts of prey
that is, his ruin would be complete, and attended with terrible miseries to the Egyptians, and afford a large booty to their enemies.
